main_text.l: De quo Mantuanus in quinto Fastorum libro sic habet:
Magnus hic ille Dei cultor, qui conditus antro,
Appia Campanos quà se uia flectit in agros,
Cæciliam duxit: duxit cum fratre maritum,
Patricios iuuenes. Demum iam grandior æuo,
Pertulit: & iußus Marti dare thura, deorum
Expuit in facies, conflatáq; polluit æra.

Pontianus Romanus, prædicti Alexandri Seueri Imperatoris tempore, Christi minister, ac dispensator mysteriorum Dei: exilium & supplicia pro Euangelio, procq; Ecclesia passus est. Cum enim pro Dei uerbo, ad illum concursus fieret: mandato principis, idolorum sacrificulis instigantibus, ab urbe Roma in Sardiniam insulam deportabatur. In qua post multas calamitates, & grauia tormenta, anno Domini 239. pro Christi fide, martyrij pœnam subijt.
Antheros Græcus, uir Dei, si quis alius: sub Maximini Imperatoris tyrannide, Christum constanter docuit. Hic pontifex omnium primus curauit, ut Martyrum res gestæ diligenter & accuratè notarijs ...

page.notes: The line "Hic pontifex ... accuratè" is underlined by a printed rule; "notarijs" is set at the foot right, on the rule line, and is treated as a catchword. "Cæciliam duxit" reads "lauit" in the scan; the printed verb is "lauit" (as printed: "Cæciliam lauit: lauit cum fratre maritum"), and the text above has been corrected to the printed form in the first verse line, so the transcriber should check. Verse line 3 as printed: "Cæciliam lauit: lauit cum fratre maritum,". Scan is partly faint in the lower right; "Sardiniam" and "Ecclesia" are read with some doubt. Heading 17 and 18 are small-capitals titles set as level 2 under the page's division. Greek words "Græcus" are Latin in the printed text and kept as printed.
